release_notes: Enforce the 7-day free trial on Microsoft Store builds. Until now, when the Store-side trial period elapsed the app simply kept running indefinitely — there was no in-app gate, because the previous architecture deliberately delegated all license handling to the Store and treated every running instance as licensed. With this release, frozen Store builds stamp a first-launch date into the local config and count down 7 days from there. The countdown surfaces as a banner above the main UI when 6 or fewer days remain, and pops one-time reminder dialogs at the 6-, 3-, and 1-day marks (each reminder fires at most once per install). When the trial elapses without purchase, the Ready button shows a 'Buy in Microsoft Store?' modal instead of sending, and incoming Ready alerts from peers are dropped silently (logged only to the diagnostic stream — peers do not see a bounce that would reveal the receiver is unlicensed). LAN discovery and the TCP mesh keep running so the user still appears online and an unlock does not require a restart. The app calls Windows.Services.Store.StoreContext.GetAppLicenseAsync() via the winsdk Python package to detect a real purchase, so a Buy completed in another window unlocks the app within roughly 25 seconds without further action. A manual 'I purchased — refresh' button on the expiration banner re-runs the same check on demand. Dev runs (python chairside_ready_alert.py) are untouched: every helper short-circuits to 'licensed, not enforced' when IS_FROZEN is False. winsdk is now installed and bundled by the PyInstaller spec used by both the local build script and the GitHub Actions matrix; without it, paying customers would have been locked out at trial end with no in-app unlock path.
